topic: effective identification strength and the matched minimax confidence-set-length frontier for the transported complier average causal effect: in the two-sample generalizability-with-noncompliance model of Chen-Huang arXiv:2506.00149 (n study draws of (X,Z,D,Y) with Y in [0,1], D and Z binary, propensity in [eps,1-eps], exclusion, monotonicity, cross-population conditional exchangeability, plus N target-population covariate draws, N/n -> c), with estimand theta_T = E_T[Delta_Y(X)]/E_T[Delta_D(X)] whose parameter space Theta = [-1,1] is FORCED compact by bounded Y and binary D, fix an envelope k_n -> infinity with k_n = o(n^(1/2)) and define the class by E_S[w]=1, w <= 2k_n a.s. and kappa_n = E_S[w^2] <= k_n, the Kish effective sample size n_eff = n/kappa_n, and the effective identification strength t_n = n_eff * mu_n^2 = n mu_n^2/kappa_n where mu_n = E_T[Delta_D(X)] is the transported first stage and both mu_n -> 0 and kappa_n -> infinity are permitted at arbitrary joint rates; calling a procedure SEQUENCE honest when liminf_n inf_P P(theta_T in C_n) >= 1-alpha and setting R(C,t_0) = limsup_n sup over {t_n >= t_0} of E_P[lambda(C_n)] and V*(t_0) = inf over honest (w,e)-oracle sequences of R(C,t_0), prove (K1) the converse V*(t_0) >= c min(1,t_0^(-1/2)) against oracles told w and e but NOT Delta_D or Delta_Y, with c depending only on alpha and the class constants and not on how t_0 splits into a first-stage/dispersion pair, hence a threshold t_c(alpha) below which every honest procedure is uninformative, and (K2) matched attainment by a single honest sequence from grid inversion over Theta of level-alpha tests of the transported moment restriction, achieving R(C,t_0) <= C min(1,t_0^(-1/2)) simultaneously for all t_0 - so the joint weak-first-stage and weak-overlap difficulty depends on (n,mu_n,kappa_n) ONLY through t = n mu_n^2/kappa_n and generalization-weight dispersion costs exactly a Kish sample-size deflation and no more - and (K3) that the same order is attained WITHOUT knowing the transport weight on the finite-cell sub-class N_n (X in a known {1,...,k_n}, P_S the known uniform law, e a known constant, only the cell vector P_T unknown, Delta_D and Delta_Y unrestricted), where K1 already holds; the test statistic and its calibration, all constants including c, C and t_c(alpha), the studentization, the bounded/unbounded/disconnected shape taxonomy, and every extension of K3 beyond N_n are explicitly DELEGATED and not pre-committed; well-posedness rests on Theta = [-1,1] being forced rather than chosen, which is exactly the infinite-diameter hypothesis the Dufour 1997 / Gleser-Hwang 1987 / Bertanha-Moreira impossibility requires and which fails here, and the literature contains no finite minimax length rate under weak identification at all; distinct from Aronow-Chang-Lopatto Biometrika 2026 (finite-population LATE, no reweighting), from Ma arXiv:2302.09756 and Smucler et al arXiv:2506.10449 (single-population weak-IV-robust LATE with ML nuisances, no covariate shift, no length theorem), and from Ren arXiv:2512.23854 (within-population MTE extrapolation on a strong-overlap space); witness: X uniform on {1,...,k_n} under P_S, P_T mass 1-eps_n on cell k_n, e = 1/2, complier probability 1/2 off the last cell and eps_n on it, no defiers, compliers with (Y(1),Y(0)) = (1,0), giving E_S[w] = 1 exactly, kappa_n <= k_n, study first stage -> 1/2 but mu_n of order (3/2)eps_n -> 0, and t_n of order (9/4) n eps_n^2/k_n tunable to any t_0; consumers are the anchor's own deep-canvassing application, Rudolph and van der Laan JRSS-B 2017 transporting the Moving to Opportunity complier effect, and Ross et al Epidemiology 2026

open_problems.open_problem: What is the minimax worst-case expected length of sequence-honest confidence sets for the compact transported CACE when the transported first stage vanishes and transport-weight dispersion diverges jointly?

source_refs.claim: Chen and Huang identify the target CACE as a transported Wald ratio and derive regular asymptotics for weighted estimators, but do not give weak-identification-uniform confidence-set length rates.
source_refs.author: Zhongren Chen and Melody Huang

source_refs.claim: Their single-population LATE score-inversion set is uniformly valid with arbitrarily weak instruments and may have infinite diameter; they give fixed-law diameter efficiency and set shapes, not a compact-parameter minimax length rate.
source_refs.author: Ezequiel Smucler, Ludovico Lanni, and David Masip

source_refs.claim: Mikusheva studies weak-IV test inversion and nearly shortest expected arc length in a linear-IV invariant model, including intersection with fixed compact intervals, but not a nonparametric transported-LATE minimax frontier.
source_refs.author: Anna Mikusheva

source_refs.claim: Dufour's positive-probability unboundedness result applies to an unbounded locally almost unidentified parameter and does not determine finite minimax length for an intrinsically compact causal ratio.
source_refs.author: Jean-Marie Dufour

source_refs.excerpt: formulate its target as a matching honest-diameter theorem against thm:diameter-lower.
No finite-sample continuous-law coverage, Poisson limit, all-regime upper frontier ... is asserted.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The published literature establishes transported-CACE identification and regular asymptotics, single-population weak-IV score inversion, and impossibility for unbounded near-unidentified parameters as separate pieces. The prior CausalSmith ratio run likewise obtained only separate Gaussian-shell conjectures and expressly withheld a matching all-regime diameter theorem. What is missing is a two-direction local experiment whose numerator and denominator perturbations obey bounded outcomes, monotonicity, covariate shift, and the weight envelope, together with one uniformly valid inversion whose expected length matches that experiment. Intrinsic compactness removes the infinite-diameter conclusion but supplies neither a finite lower rate nor attainment.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A same-class lower bound and a single uniformly honest test-inversion sequence proving the compact transported-CACE expected-length frontier min{1,t_0^(-1/2)}, including a constant-order uninformative phase.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the exact policy motivation, two-sample data structure, transported complier estimand, and deep-canvassing application that the new problem must preserve.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: noncompliance makes transported ITT insufficient -> the target-population complier effect is a transported Wald ratio -> weak compliance and dispersed transport weights can jointly erase precision -> determine the compact-parameter minimax confidence-set-length frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Invert a studentized orthogonal score for a ratio estimand and prove uniform validity under triangular weak-instrument sequences, including nonstandard ratio limits.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Transported CACE is also a ratio whose null is a linear moment in the candidate parameter; this is the closest nonparametric weak-LATE inversion proof.

method_exemplars.technique: Compare inverted weak-IV tests by expected length after intersecting with a fixed compact parameter interval, using uniform asymptotics and invariant testing.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly treats expected confidence-set length under weak identification and explicitly studies compact truncation.

method_exemplars.technique: Use modulus and least-favourable-pair arguments to derive honest minimax interval lower bounds under deteriorating overlap.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target resolution also needs an honest-length lower bound whose information deteriorates with overlap.

open_problems.open_problem: What necessary-and-sufficient nuisance-learning boundary governs whether a single feasible transported-CACE procedure can retain oracle coverage and effective-strength length across all joint weak-first-stage and weak-overlap sequences?

source_refs.claim: Ma constructs a high-dimensional DML-based LATE test with uniformly correct asymptotic size irrespective of identification strength, but the model is single-population and has no transport-weight dispersion.
source_refs.author: Yukun Ma
source_refs.venue: arXiv preprint; R&R at Journal of Econometrics

source_refs.claim: Their weak-instrument triangular-array validity requires empirical-process and nuisance-bias terms to be negligible, while the usual doubly robust LATE estimator has a nonnormal weak-IV limit.
source_refs.author: Ezequiel Smucler, Ludovico Lanni, and David Masip

source_refs.claim: Chen and Huang propose weighted and multiply robust estimators for target CACE and regular sandwich/Wald inference, but do not give nuisance-rate conditions uniform over jointly shrinking compliance and deteriorating transport overlap.
source_refs.author: Zhongren Chen and Melody Huang

source_refs.excerpt: Sharpen the all-regime conjecture into a necessary-and-sufficient smoothness--rarity frontier
Necessity of rare-learning inequalities and bounded-count diameter are open questions.

open_problems.why_unsolved: At regular laws, orthogonality and cross-fitting control first-order nuisance error. A shrinking transported first stage magnifies any remaining numerator or denominator bias, while diverging transport weights enlarge empirical-process norms and make random studentization less stable. The prior ratio proposal assumed rare-scale learning inequalities but supplied no necessity result, and the transport and weak-LATE papers address only one side of this interaction. Thus effective strength alone may cease to characterize feasible inference once outcome, compliance, propensity, and transport nuisances must all be learned.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A cross-fitted test-inversion theorem with explicit sufficient nuisance rates, paired with a testing lower bound outside that region, yielding an if-and-only-if smoothness-effective-strength boundary or a quantified adaptation penalty.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation directly connects high-dimensional nuisance learning, weak identification, and test inversion, requiring only a pivot to two-sample transport.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: modern LATE analyses use high-dimensional covariates -> Wald/DML inference fails under weak instruments -> orthogonal test inversion restores size -> determine exactly when the same adaptation survives unknown transport and weak overlap

method_exemplars.technique: Cross-fit high-dimensional nuisances inside an identification-robust conditional test and invert the test rather than studentizing a ratio estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves nuisance learning plus weak-LATE inference in one population; the missing terms come from the target sample and transport weights.

method_exemplars.technique: Track score-inversion and nuisance remainders along weak-instrument triangular arrays and derive the nonnormal ratio limit of the plug-in estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its triangular-array remainder conditions identify what must be rescaled when importance weights also diverge.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine doubly robust transport scores, rate calculations, higher-order correction, and minimax lower bounds for target functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the target-sample nuisance decomposition absent from single-population weak-IV procedures.

open_problems.open_problem: At bounded or transition-scale effective strength for transported CACE, what least-favourable experiment and calibration give honest confidence sets, and how accurately does a finite-profile law approximate its Poisson or Gaussian limit?

source_refs.excerpt: an explicit least-favourable profile characterization or a quantitative finite-to-Poisson approximation bound.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The rejected compact-ratio angle supplied finite randomized calibration only inside an abstract profile experiment and a separate Gaussian-shell score result. It did not construct measurable least-favourable continuous profiling, prove finite-to-Poisson transfer, or control expected length after unconditioning. Transported CACE adds the compatibility constraints imposed by monotonicity and a target-weighted denominator, so it is unknown whether the same finite experiment governs every split of effective strength into first-stage weakness and weight dispersion.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit least-favourable conditional experiment, a measurable level-alpha test, and a quantitative deficiency or coupling bound transferring coverage and expected length across bounded-strength, transition, and Gaussian regimes.

writing_exemplar.why: Its rare-event uncertainty-quantification framing is a close narrative template for why Gaussian calibration can fail and a discrete transition experiment is needed.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: few effectively informative observations defeat normal calibration -> finite or Poisson experiments retain the relevant information -> ratio inversion must be calibrated in that transition -> characterize honest transported-CACE sets across all effective-strength regimes

method_exemplars.technique: Profile and invert a weak-identification-robust statistic with uniform size control rather than rely on a Wald approximation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems require validity when the informative component is small and Gaussian studentization is unstable.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct ratio confidence sets by geometric inversion while retaining nonstandard set shapes under a weak denominator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The transported set is also obtained by inverting a ratio moment across denominator-strength regimes.

open_problems.open_problem: Is the transport-weight second moment, through Kish effective sample size, a sufficient index of joint weak-overlap and weak-first-stage difficulty for transported-CACE inference, or can higher weight moments and target-sample geometry change the minimax length rate at fixed t?

source_refs.claim: Polo and Vicente describe the formal relationship among effective sample size, dimensionality, and covariate-shift generalization as obscure and develop a learning-theoretic account, not a causal-ratio confidence-set equivalence theorem.
source_refs.author: Felipe Maia Polo and Renato Vicente

source_refs.claim: Li, Lam, and Prusty show that importance weighting has high variance under large source-target discrepancy and propose a control-variate combination with regression; their rates are prediction rates, not a transported causal-ratio information frontier.
source_refs.author: Fengpei Li, Henry Lam, and Siddharth Prusty

source_refs.claim: Chen and Huang use inverse transport weights in target-CACE estimation and derive regular asymptotics, but do not establish that weight dispersion enters weak-identification risk only through its second moment.
source_refs.author: Zhongren Chen and Melody Huang

open_problems.why_unsolved: The literature supports Kish ESS as a variance diagnostic and documents instability of importance weighting, but it does not establish asymptotic equivalence of transported-CACE experiments sharing n*mu^2/E[w^2]. A proof must control triangular arrays with diverging maximum weights and rule out Lindeberg failure, sparse target cells, and nonlinear ratio effects. A refutation must instead keep the first stage and second moment fixed while changing only higher-order weight geometry and prove a different honest-length risk.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either an information-equivalence theorem reducing minimax risk to t=n*mu^2/E[w^2], or two admissible sequences with the same t but provably different minimax confidence-set-length orders.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation is organized around the unresolved meaning of effective sample size under covariate shift, which pivots cleanly into the causal weak-identification question.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: covariate shift motivates importance weighting -> unequal weights reduce effective sample size -> ESS is widely used but its formal sufficiency is unclear -> determine whether Kish ESS alone indexes transported-CACE information

method_exemplars.technique: Decompose covariate-shift error into regression and weighted-residual components and control them with a control variate.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The decomposition isolates the component attributable to weights and can test whether second-moment dispersion is exhaustive.

method_exemplars.technique: Use modulus-of-continuity lower bounds to characterize when overlap geometry controls honest interval length.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This machinery can compare same-ESS designs with potentially different local moduli.

open_problems.open_problem: Can transported-CACE confidence sets retain the oracle effective-strength length rate when transport weights are estimated from a separate target covariate sample, first on growing finite-cell models and then on stated nonparametric covariate classes?

source_refs.claim: Chen and Huang derive consistency and asymptotic distributions for weighted target-CACE estimators with an unknown modeled selection mechanism under regular conditions, not joint weak-first-stage and diverging-weight sequences.
source_refs.author: Zhongren Chen and Melody Huang

source_refs.claim: Rudolph and van der Laan derive efficient-influence-function inference and TMLEs for transported encouragement-design CACE and report practical positivity difficulties, but do not give minimax length rates under vanishing compliance and growing transport dispersion.
source_refs.author: Kara E. Rudolph and Mark J. van der Laan
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B

source_refs.claim: Zeng et al. derive doubly robust transported-ATE rates, limiting distributions, efficiency, local asymptotic minimaxity, and minimax lower bounds under regularity, but not a weak ratio estimand with diverging density-ratio dispersion.
source_refs.author: Zhenghao Zeng, Edward H. Kennedy, Lisa M. Bodnar, and Ashley I. Naimi

open_problems.why_unsolved: Regular transported-effect theory handles estimated sampling scores through influence-function expansions. With a vanishing transported first stage, weight-estimation error is divided by a shrinking denominator, and growing finite cells can make target probabilities sparse. The unresolved issue is whether orthogonalization or balancing absorbs that error uniformly at the oracle rate, or whether estimating the target density ratio creates a separate N-dependent information bottleneck.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An oracle-equivalence theorem for a feasible weight-learning and score-inversion procedure on a stated growing-cell class, together with a lower bound locating any N-dependent separation regime and any extension boundary beyond finite cells.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents unknown selection weights as the practical version of transported-CACE estimation, so its setup leads directly to the oracle-versus-feasible question.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: target CACE requires reweighting study conditional effects -> target covariate data identify selection weights -> regular plug-in theory estimates those weights -> ask whether weight learning remains costless when overlap and compliance weaken jointly

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate retargeted means with minimax linear balancing weights and prove finite-sample error bounds and asymptotic inference without direct density-ratio plug-in.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each transported reduced-form moment is a retargeted mean, so the machinery can be applied before weak-ratio inversion.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct transported-CACE TMLEs from efficient influence functions that combine target-distribution and source conditional-effect information.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the exact two-sample efficient-score decomposition whose remainder must be made uniform over weak first stages and deteriorating overlap.

method_exemplars.technique: Correct a regression plug-in by a minimax linear estimate of its error and prove efficiency through Riesz-representer approximation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is an orthogonal route to transported numerator and denominator moments when direct density-ratio estimation is unstable.

open_problems.open_problem: What bounded, disconnected, empty, or full-parameter-space shapes can compact transported-CACE score confidence sets have, and can every component be computed without grid truncation while preserving weak-identification-uniform coverage?

source_refs.claim: Smucler, Lanni, and Masip characterize six possible score-confidence-set forms for nonparametric single-population LATE on an unbounded parameter space.
source_refs.author: Ezequiel Smucler, Ludovico Lanni, and David Masip

source_refs.claim: Schlemper and Moreira show that routine grid inversion can miss components or truncate unbounded weak-IV confidence regions and derive exact polynomial or rational inversion algorithms for linear-IV statistics.
source_refs.author: Gustavo Schlemper and Marcelo J. Moreira

source_refs.claim: Aronow, Chang, and Lopatto obtain finite-sample-exact studentized Anderson-Rubin sets under homogeneous effects and asymptotically valid finite-population LATE sets under heterogeneity, in a non-transported randomization model.
source_refs.author: P. M. Aronow, Haoge Chang, and Patrick Lopatto

open_problems.why_unsolved: The single-population score statistic has a tractable acceptance inequality, but transport adds target-sample variation, estimated weights, and potentially candidate-dependent studentization. Intersecting with an intrinsically compact parameter space changes the unbounded taxonomy, while a finite grid can miss narrow or disconnected accepted components. No cited paper gives a topology and exact inversion theorem for this two-sample transported moment.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An analytic classification of every compact transported-score confidence-set topology plus a certified root-finding or adaptive-inversion algorithm whose numerical error is proved not to affect uniform coverage.

writing_exemplar.why: Its exposition is organized around score-set geometry, fixed-law diameter, and weak-instrument behavior.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: score inversion gives weak-IV validity -> inversion can produce qualitatively different set shapes -> transport and compactness alter the acceptance geometry -> classify and compute every possible transported-CACE set

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce the squared studentized-score inequality to coefficient and discriminant cases and enumerate the resulting set topology.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The transported null moment remains affine in the candidate parameter, so analogous discriminant analysis may survive the two-sample variance.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert polynomial and rational weak-identification statistics by certified root finding rather than a finite grid.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly addresses the computational failure mode and offers a transferable exact-inversion strategy.

open_problems.open_problem: Under bounded violations of cross-population adherence or compliance exchangeability, what is the sharp sensitivity identified set for transported CACE and how does its honest confidence-set length interact with effective identification strength?

source_refs.claim: Ross et al. show that target mean outcomes are not identified when trial participation changes adherence and target adherence data are unavailable, and propose sensitivity analysis indexed by relative adherence differences.
source_refs.author: Rachael K. Ross, Iván Díaz, Amy J. Pitts, Elizabeth A. Stuart, and Kara E. Rudolph

source_refs.claim: Dahabreh, Robertson, and Hernán give examples where nonadherence makes target assignment effects nonidentified because trial engagement affects receipt or participation shares unmeasured causes with receipt.
source_refs.author: Issa J. Dahabreh, Sarah E. Robertson, and Miguel A. Hernán

source_refs.claim: Chen and Huang introduce sensitivity analysis around target-CACE transport, but do not combine sensitivity-set width with weak-first-stage and weak-overlap honest-inference rates.
source_refs.author: Zhongren Chen and Melody Huang

open_problems.why_unsolved: The literature shows that adherence shifts can destroy point identification and offers sensitivity parameters and regular estimators. It does not characterize the sharp target-CACE identified set under a bounded violation class or separate irreducible sensitivity width from sampling width when the transported first stage is weak and weights are dispersed. The same compliance mechanism enters both the ratio denominator and the sensitivity restriction, coupling partial-identification and weak-identification nonregularities.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp bound formula for transported CACE under an explicit adherence-shift sensitivity class and a uniformly valid confidence region whose length separates identified-set width from an effective-strength sampling term.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation starts from the practical transport failure caused by trial-induced adherence and proceeds directly to sensitivity analysis.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: trial procedures can change adherence -> target adherence data may be absent -> target outcomes cease to be point identified -> derive sharp transported-CACE sensitivity bounds and honest weak-strength inference

method_exemplars.technique: Parameterize conditional relative adherence differences across populations and propagate the sensitivity parameter through transported counterfactual means.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a domain-native restriction on the transport failure that must be converted into a sharp CACE identified set.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert a weak-identification-robust score over candidate ratio values rather than rely on a Wald expansion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After profiling over the sensitivity class, score inversion can protect coverage when the compliance denominator approaches zero.

literature_map:
1. Chen and Huang (2025, arXiv:2506.00149) identify target CACE as a transported Wald ratio and derive weighted and multiply robust regular asymptotics; no weak-ID minimax-length theorem is stated.
2. Rudolph and van der Laan (2017, JRSSB, DOI 10.1111/rssb.12213) give EIF/TMLE inference for transported encouragement-design CACE and document practical positivity problems.
3. Clark et al. (2024, arXiv:2405.04419) develop transported principal-stratum effects, nonparametric efficiency theory, and efficient estimators under principal-stratification assumptions.
4. Dahabreh, Robertson, and Hernán (2022, arXiv:2211.04876) show that nonadherence can make transported assignment effects nonidentified when engagement affects receipt or unmeasured adherence factors select trial participation.
5. Ross et al. (2026, Epidemiology, DOI 10.1097/EDE.0000000000001925) address trial-induced adherence shifts with sensitivity analysis, not weak-ID length theory.
6. Ma (2023, arXiv:2302.09756) gives DML-based identification-robust LATE test inversion with high-dimensional covariates in one population.
7. Smucler, Lanni, and Masip (2025, arXiv:2506.10449) establish weak-IV-uniform score-set validity, six set shapes, fixed-law diameter efficiency, and nonnormal DRML limits; their parameter space is not the compact transported model.
8. Aronow, Chang, and Lopatto (2026, Biometrika, DOI 10.1093/biomet/asag010) give studentized AR randomization confidence sets for finite-population LATE without transport weighting.
9. Mikusheva (2010, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2009.12.003) studies weak-IV test inversion and expected length, including intersection with fixed compact intervals, in linear IV.
10. Dufour (1997), Gleser-Hwang (1987), and Bertanha-Moreira (2020) give unbounded-parameter or near-unidentified impossibility results; intrinsic compactness removes the infinite-diameter conclusion but does not supply a finite minimax rate.
11. Polo and Vicente (2023, DOI 10.1007/s00521-021-06615-1) frame the formal link among Kish ESS, dimension, and covariate-shift performance as obscure; Li, Lam, and Prusty (2020, AISTATS) analyze variance inflation and robust weighting.
12. Zeng et al. (2024, arXiv:2302.00092), Hirshberg, Maleki, and Zubizarreta (2019, arXiv:1901.10296), and Hirshberg and Wager (2021, DOI 10.1214/21-AOS2080) provide regular minimax or efficient transport and retargeted-mean machinery.
13. Armstrong and Kolesár (2021, Econometrica, DOI 10.3982/ECTA16907) give honest minimax intervals under deteriorating overlap via modulus and bias-aware methods, but not for a transported weak ratio.
14. Schlemper and Moreira (2026, arXiv:2604.04279) show finite grids can miss or truncate weak-IV confidence regions and provide exact inversion algorithms; extending this geometry to compact transported scores remains open.
15. The central cross-literature tension is componentwise: transport papers are regular, weak-IV papers omit covariate shift, overlap papers omit weak causal ratios, and impossibility papers use unbounded or different parameter spaces.
